learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and appropriately apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Capacity and skill to plan and carry out experimental research, interpret results, and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes, and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Ability to collect and interpret data and handle complex concepts within their specialty, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Relates material transformation manufacturing processes with product specifications.
Knows and applies procedures for calculating manufacturing process costs.
Plans and designs part manufacturing processes, identifies and proposes necessary manufacturing installations/cells and tooling to optimize costs and quality.
Drafts the documentation corresponding to the manufacturing process of a mechanical component or assembly.

syllabus_topics: PRODUCT COST STRUCTURE. TYPES OF COSTS
MACHINING AND ASSEMBLY PLANT ORGANIZATION PROJECT
teaching_methods: Lectures, participatory classes (teacher's presentation in class of concepts and procedures)
Performance of exercises individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on individual written and oral tests for technical competencies, and reports from exercises, case studies, computer, simulation, and laboratory practices. For each activity, a 100% weight is indicated, implying comprehensive evaluation of specific competencies rather than a proportional contribution to an overall course grade. The recovery mechanism for all assessed activities is individual written and oral tests for technical competencies of the subject.
